rationale:
Evidence: iteration 9 (score 531.7, best so far) is the iteration 5 design with mass lowered from 0.5 to 0.4 kg. It finishes the oval 20/20 at 2.11 s, s-bend progress rose from 0.78 to 0.82 (6/20 finishes), and slalom is essentially unchanged at 0.38 (0/20). Every failure is off_track with max_error 0.054 to 0.064 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m limit. Steering oscillation is moderate (0.25 to 0.51), with the highest value on the s-bend. The robot lags behind bends rather than jittering. Iterations 3 and 4 showed that stiffer loops (higher kp, ki) hurt the oval, and iterations 6 and 7 showed that changing sensor span or base_speed away from 1.1 hurts. Mass was a small, positive effect, so I keep it at 0.4.

Change (one variable, controller only): kd 0.6 -> 0.8. Derivative action adds phase lead, so the robot should react to the approaching edge of the tape sooner in each bend. This tests whether the remaining lag comes from missing damping. Sensors, gains kp and ki, base_speed, geometry and line_loss are all unchanged from iteration 9, so any change in s-bend and slalom progress can be read as a derivative effect.

Expected result: s-bend progress 0.85 or more with 7 or more finishes, slalom progress rising toward 0.45, and oval finishes holding at 20/20. Steering oscillation may rise somewhat, but should stay below about 0.5.

Hypotheses: H1, extra kd reduces the lag-driven max_error on bends. H2, the oval holds because the straight-line behaviour is dominated by kp and does not change. H3, if steering_oscillation rises above 0.5 without a gain in progress, kd is too high and the optimum lies between 0.6 and 0.8.

Next measurements: completion and progress per track (whether slalom finishes at all), max_error and rms_error (is the lag reduced), steering_oscillation (is the derivative amplifying jitter), line_loss_events (dropouts on tight bends), and completion_time.
